The meaning of their nasb of yā’unu dead was the meaning of the first two, and they made it feminine to make it feminine, just as one says: innahu qayma’ jayyidati your slave girl, and innahu qayma’ jayyidati your slave girl, so the unknown is mentioned once and made feminine another time, to make the noun that comes after it feminine. Some of the Medinans read it as: illa an yakunu except that it is dead, with the ta’ in yā’unu to be, and with a shaddah on the yā’ from yā’unu dead, and with its raf’ higher case, so they made yā’unu dead the noun of yā’unu dead, and they made yā’unu dead the feminine of yā’unu dead, and they made yā’unu suffice with the noun without the verb, because his saying: illa an yakunu ya’unu except that it is dead, is an exception, and the Arabs are satisfied with nouns instead of verbs in making an exception, so they say: the people stood up, illa an yā’u akhāka he is your brother, and illa an yā’u akhūka he is your brother, so they do not use d yā’un as a verb, and they make it independent of the noun, just as one says: the people stood up, illa an akhāka he is your brother, and illa an akhūka he is your brother, so the noun that comes after the letter of exception is not lacking a verb. Abu Ja`far said: The correct reading of this in my opinion is: except that it is with the letter ya “dead,” with the letter ya softened and the word dead in the accusative case, because what is in it is is from the implied mention of the masculine, and it is: Say, I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who eats it unless it is a dead animal or blood poured forth. As for reading dead woman in the nominative case, since it is not wrong in Arabic, then the reading in this place is not correct. Because God says: or blood poured out, there is no disagreement among everyone in reading blood in the accusative case, and this is also the case in the copies of the Muslims’ Qur’ans, and it is in apposition to dead woman. So since that is the case, it is known that if dead woman were in the nominative case, then the blood and His saying: or transgression would be in the nominative case, but they are in the accusative case, so they are in apposition to it in the accusative case. Abu Ja`far said: We have mentioned the difference of opinion among the people of interpretation in the interpretation of His statement: But whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor exceeding [its limits], and the correct statement regarding it, according to us, is what has preceded in this book of ours, in Surat al-Baqarah, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place, and that its meaning is: So whoever is forced to eat what God has forbidden, such as eating dead animals, spilled blood, or pork, or that which has been dedicated to other than God, not desiring to eat it out of enjoyment, not out of necessity due to a state of hunger, nor exceeding in eating it by exceeding what God has set and permitted him to eat, that is, he eats from it what will remove the fear for himself from dying by not eating it, he does not exceed that to more than that, so there is no blame upon him for eating what he has eaten of that, for God is Forgiving, in what he did of that, so He covered it up for him by not punishing him for it, and if He had willed, He would have punished him for it, Merciful, in permitting him to eat that when he needed it, and if He had willed, He would have forbidden it to him and prevented him from it.
6:146: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And We have forbidden the Jews, everything with claws, which is from the beasts and birds unless it has split toes, such as camels, ostriches, geese, and ducks. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Muthanna and Ali bin Dawud told me, they said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying: And to those who are Jews, We have forbidden every animal having claws, meaning the camel and the ostrich. Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas: And to those who are Jews We have forbidden all animals having claws, he said: the camel, the ostrich, and similar animals. Ibn Wakee` told us, he said, Yahya ibn Adam told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of `Ata`, on the authority of Sa`id: And to those who are Jews We have forbidden all animals having claws, he said: it is that which does not have open fingers. Ali bin Al-Hussein Al-Azdi told me, he said, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Saib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement: And We have forbidden to those who are Jews every animal having claws, he said: Everything with separate digits, including the rooster. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: Everything with claws means the ostrich and the camel. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, similarly. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Sa`id told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And to those who are Jews We have forbidden every animal having claws, so it was said: the camel, the ostrich, and similar birds and whales. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada: Everything with claws, he said: camels and ostriches, the claws of the camel’s hand and foot, and the ostrich is also like that. And what was also forbidden to them from the birds was ducks and the like, and everything that does not have split toes. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: As for everything with claws, it refers to camels and ostriches. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sheikh told us, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And to those who are Jews, We have forbidden every animal having claws, he said: The ostrich and the camel, split in two. I said: What is split in two? He said: Everything whose legs are not spread out, the Jews did not eat, and the camel and the ostrich. And the chickens and sparrows, the Jews eat, because they have spread out. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: Everything having claws, he said: The ostrich and the camel, split in two. I said to Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza, and he told me: What is split in two? He said: Everything that has not spread out from the hooves of animals. He said: And whatever has spread out, the Jews eat. He said: The legs of chickens and sparrows have spread out, so the Jews eat them. He said: The camel’s hoof, its hoof, and the ostrich’s hoof, and the hoof of the hyena, and the hoof of the hyena, are not separated. So the Jews do not eat camels, ostriches, or hyenas, nor anything whose hoof is not separated. Likewise, they do not eat a wild donkey. Ibn Zayd used to say about that as follows: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And We have forbidden to those who are Jews every animal with claws, meaning camels. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion that we mentioned on the authority of Ibn `Abbas and those who said something similar to his statement. Because God, the Most High, has informed us that He has forbidden the Jews everything with claws, so it is not permissible to exclude something that has died from the generality of this report except what the people of knowledge have agreed is excluded from it. If that is the case, and the ostrich and everything that is not from the beasts and birds that has claws other than open toes is included in the apparent meaning of the revelation, then it must be ruled that it is included in the report, since it did not come that some of that is not included in the verse, a report from God or from His Messenger, and the majority of the nation agreed that it is included in it. Abu Jaafar said: The people of interpretation differed regarding the fats that God Almighty said that He forbade the Jews from cows and sheep. Some of them said: They are the fats of sheep specifically. Those who said that mentioned: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And of the cattle and the sheep We have forbidden them their fat, the fat. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: May God fight the Jews, God forbade them the fat, then they ate its price. Others said: Rather, it was any fat that was not mixed with bone or on bone. Those who said that mentioned: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said, regarding his statement: We have forbidden them their fat, he said: What was forbidden to them was the omentum, and all fat was like that except in a bone. Others said: Rather, it is the fat of the omentum and kidneys. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement: We have forbidden them their fat, he said: the omentum and the fat of the kidneys. The Jews used to say: Israel only forbade it, so we forbid it. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement: We have forbidden them their fat, he said: He only forbade them the urinary tract and the kidneys. This is how it is in my book on the authority of Yunus, and I think that it is: the kidneys. Abu Ja`far said: The correct statement in this regard is to say: God informed us that He had forbidden the Jews the fat of cows and sheep, except for what He had excluded from them, such as what their backs carried, or what was in their entrails, or what was mixed with a bone. So all fat, other than what God had excluded in His Book from cows and sheep, was forbidden to them. And similar to this statement, the report of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has been reported, and that is his saying: May God fight the Jews, the fat was forbidden to them, so they rendered it, then sold it and ate its price. As for his saying: Except what their backs carry, he means: except the fat of the sides and what is attached to the back, for it is not forbidden to them. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Except what their backs carry, meaning: what is attached to the back of the fat. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us on the authority of Al-Suddi: As for what their backs carried, it means the buttocks. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Saleh, he said: The buttocks are what their backs carry. Abu Jaafar said: Al-Hawaya is a plural, the singular of which is Hawiya, Hawiya, and Hawiya. It is what is contained in the stomach, so it gathers and becomes round. They are the daughters of milk, and they are the camels, and they are called the resting places, and they contain the intestines. The meaning of the statement is: And from the cows and the sheep, We have forbidden them their fat, except what their backs burn, or what the intestines carry. So Al-Hawaya is in the nominative case, in apposition to the back, and ma that comes after illa is in the accusative case as an exception from the fat. And the people of interpretation said the same as we said about that. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Or the Hawaya, which is the Ma’bar. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: or the depths, he said: the grave. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Al-Hawaya means the resting place and the den. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Shibl, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Or the surroundings, he said: the spring. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Sameed bin Jubair: Or the camels, he said: the camels. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: Or the camels, he said: the camels. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada. Or the Hawaya, he said: the Ma’bar. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Or the Hawaya, he said: the Ma’bar. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah and Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said: Al-Mubar. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: or the insides, meaning the bellies other than the stomachs. Muhammad bin Saad Qal` told me, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying: or the surroundings, it is the burial place. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Or the camels, he said: the camels. Ibn Zayd said about this: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement: or the chambers, he said: The chambers are the resting places where the intestines are, they are in the middle, and they are the daughters of milk, and in the speech of the Arabs they are called resting places. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And of the cattle and the sheep We have forbidden to those who are Jews their fat, except for what their backs carry, or what their entrails carry, for We have made that lawful for them. Otherwise, what is mixed with a bone is also lawful for them. He responded to his statement: or what was mixed with a bone, with his statement: except what their backs carried, so the ma in his statement: or what was mixed with a bone, is in the accusative case in apposition to the ma in his statement: except what their backs carried. And he meant by his statement: or what was mixed with a bone, the fat of the buttocks and flanks, and the like, as in: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: Or what is mixed with a bone, he said: The fat of the buttocks with the coccyx, so it is permissible. And everything in the legs, side, head, and eye that is mixed with a bone, so it is permissible. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Or what is mixed with a bone, which is fat on a bone. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: This is what We have forbidden to the Jews of livestock and birds with ungulates, and of cows and sheep, what We have forbidden to them of their fat, which We mentioned in this verse, We have forbidden it to them as a punishment from Us to them, and as a reward for their evil deeds and their transgression against their Lord, as: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: That is how We recompensed them for their transgression, and indeed, We are truthful. This was only forbidden to them as punishment for their transgression. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, That is how We recompensed them for their transgression, that is, We did that to them for their transgression. And His statement, And indeed, we are truthful, he says, and indeed, we are truthful in our report about these Jews regarding what We forbade them of the fats and meat of cattle and birds which We mentioned that We forbade them, and in other reports of ours. And they are the liars in their claim that Israel only forbade it for himself, and that they only forbade it because Israel forbade it for himself.
6:147: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: If you, Muhammad, have lied to these Jews in what we have told you, we have forbidden them and permitted them, as we have explained in this verse, Then say, your Lord is full of mercy, to us, and to those of His servants who believe in Him, and to others of His creation, vast, encompassing all of His creation, the good and the bad. He does not hasten to punish those who disbelieve in Him, nor to punish those who disobey Him, nor does He neglect the honor of those who believe in Him and obey Him, nor does He deprive them of the reward for their deeds, out of mercy from Him to both groups. But His wrath, which is His power and His torment, does not repel it when He permits it when He is angry with the criminals, and the criminals are those who committed crimes and acquired sins and perpetrated evil deeds. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: If they deny you, meaning the Jews. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: If they deny you, meaning the Jews, then say, ‘Your Lord is the possessor of vast mercy.’ Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: The Jews used to say: Israel only forbade it - meaning the omentum and the fat of the kidneys - so we forbid it, and that is what He said: But if they deny you, then say, ‘Your Lord is full of vast mercy, and His punishment cannot be averted from the criminal people.’
6:148: Abu Ja`far said: The Most High says: Those who associate others with God will say, and they are the idols and statues among the polytheists of Quraysh, If God had willed, we would not have associated others with Him, meaning: They said, in order to prevent submission to the truth by falsehood from the argument, when the truth was made clear to them, and they knew the falsehood of what they were established upon in their polytheism, and their prohibition of what they were prohibiting of crops and livestock, as the Most High had explained in the previous verses before that: And they assigned to God a share of what He created of crops and livestock, and what comes after that: If God had wanted us to believe in Him, and to single Him out for worship without the idols and deities, and to make permissible what He had prohibited of lakes and wild animals and other than that of our wealth, we would not have made a partner for God, nor would our fathers before us have made that for Him, nor would we have prohibited what we prohibit of these things that we are established upon prohibiting, because He is able to prevent us from that, so that we would not have the ability to do anything. There is a way to do this: either by forcing us to believe and abandon associating partners with Him, and to say that what He has forbidden is permissible, or by being kind to us with His guidance, so that we come to acknowledge His Oneness, and abandon the worship of anything less than Him of rivals and idols, and to permit what He has forbidden us. But He was pleased with what we are upon of worshipping idols and statues and taking partners for Him in worship and rivals, and He wanted what we are forbidden of crops and livestock, so He did not stand between us and what we are upon of that. God said, refuting their claim that God is pleased with what we are upon of polytheism and prohibiting what we prohibit, and rejecting the falsehood of their argument in that regard, Thus did those before them deny, meaning: Just as these polytheists denied, O Muhammad, what you brought to them of truth and clarification, the wicked nations before them denied what their prophets brought to them of God’s signs and clear proofs, and rejected their advice, until they tasted Our punishment, meaning: until they angered Us, so We became angry with them, so We brought down Our punishment upon them, and they tasted it, and were ruined by their tasting of it, so they failed and lost this world and the Hereafter. He said: And these others will be led on their path, if they do not repent and believe and acknowledge what you have brought to them from their Lord. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: If God had willed, we would not have associated [anything], nor would our fathers, and he said: Thus did those before them deny, then he said: If God had willed, they would not have associated [anything], for they said: Our worship of deities brings us closer to God, so God informed them that it does not bring them closer. And His statement: If God had willed, they would not have associated [anything], God Almighty says: If God had willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And we have not forbidden anything, he said: The saying of the Quraysh, meaning: God has forbidden this bahīrah and the sā’ibah. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And we have not forbidden anything, the Quraysh said without certainty: God has forbidden this bahīrah and this sā’ibah. If someone were to say: What is your proof that God, the Most High, denied what these polytheists said, saying: God is pleased with us worshipping idols, and He wanted us to forbid what He forbade us of crops and livestock, without His denial of them being based on their saying: If God had willed, we would not have associated [anything], nor would our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything, and based on their description of Him as having willed their polytheism and the polytheism of their fathers, and their forbidding what they used to forbid? It would be said to him: The proof of that is His saying: Thus did those before them deny, so God, the Most High, informed us about them that they followed in their denial of their Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in what he brought them from God - of forbidding the worship of anything other than God, the Most High, and forbidding other than what God forbade in His Book and on the tongue of His Messenger - the same path as their ancestors from the past nations who denied God and His Messenger. And the denial from them was only for a denier, and if that was report from God about their lie in their saying: If God had willed, we would not have associated [anything], nor would our fathers, He would have said: Thus did those before them deny, with a light dhal, and He would have attributed their saying that to lying about God, not to denial, with many reasons that would take too long to mention in the book, and what we have mentioned is sufficient for whoever is guided to understand it. Abu Ja`far said: The Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these people who treat idols and statues as equals to their Lord, who forbid what they forbid of crops and livestock, who say: If God had willed, we would not have associated [anything], nor would our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything, but He was pleased with us for what we are upon of polytheism and forbidding what we forbid: Do you have - by your claim that you claim against God of His pleasure in your associating in His worship what you associate, and your forbidding from your wealth what you forbid - certain knowledge from the report of one whose report cuts off an excuse, or an argument that requires certainty for us, from knowledge, so bring it forth to us, meaning: so show it to us and clarify it, just as We have shown you the places of error in your words and actions, and the contradiction and impossibility of that in the rational and the heard, You follow nothing but conjecture, meaning He says to him: Say to them: If you say what you say, O polytheists, and worship from the idols and statues what you worship, and forbid Of the crops and livestock you forbid, except out of assumption and belief that it is true, and that you are right, and it is false, and you are wrong. And you are only guessing, He says: And you, and you are not in all of that, except guessing, He says: Except that you attribute falsehood to God, assuming without certain knowledge or clear proof.
6:149: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these people who equate idols and statues with their Lord, who say lies about their Lord, in their prohibition of what they have prohibited of crops and livestock, if they are unable to establish proof when you say to them: Do you have any knowledge of what you claim against your Lord so that you can bring it forth to us, and about bringing forth that knowledge to you and revealing it, and they are undoubtedly unable to do that, and are negligent in revealing it, because it is false and has no truth, then to God, who has forbidden you to associate anything with Him, and to follow the footsteps of Satan in your wealth of crops and livestock, is the conclusive proof, without you, O polytheists. By balighah it means that it reaches His purpose in being established for whoever among His creation uses it as evidence against Him, and it cuts off his excuse if it reaches him in what it is made an argument for. If He had willed, He would have guided you all, meaning: If your Lord had willed, He would have guided you all to agree on worshipping Him alone, disavowing rivals and gods, judging by what God has forbidden and what God has permitted, abandoning following the footsteps of Satan, and other acts of obedience to Him. However, He did not will that. So He made differences among His creation in what He willed from them, so some of them are disbelievers and some are believers. A group of the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, he said: No one has an argument for disobeying God, but God has the conclusive argument for His servants. And He said: If He had willed, He could have guided you all, he said: He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.
6:150: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these slanderers against their Lord, the idol worshippers, who claim that God has forbidden them what they have forbidden of their crops and livestock, Bring your witnesses. He says: Bring your witnesses who will testify against God that He has forbidden you what you claim He has forbidden you. The people of Al-Aliyah in Tihamah use the word halam in singular, dual and plural forms, and it is masculine and feminine. So you say to a singular person: halam ya so-and-so, and to a dual and plural likewise, and to a female likewise. From this is the saying of Al-A’sha: His call to his people, Come to your cause, had been cut short. He chants: Come on and Come on. As for the people of the lower class of Najd, they singularize for one, dualize for two, and pluralize for all. So it is said to one man: Come on, to one woman: Come on, to two al-Nas 114:Come on, to a group of men: Come on, and to women: Come on. God said to His Prophet: If they bear witness, meaning: O Muhammad, if they bring you witnesses who testify that God has forbidden what they claim God has forbidden them, then do not bear witness with them, for they are liars and false witnesses in their testimony to what they have testified to about that against God. And He, the Most High, addressed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant by that are his companions and the believers in him, And do not follow the inclinations of those who deny Our revelations, meaning: And do not follow them in what they are upon of denying the revelation of God and His sending down, in forbidding what He has forbidden, and permitting what He has permitted for them, but follow what has been revealed to you from the Book of your Lord, which falsehood cannot approach from before it or from behind it, And those who do not believe in the Hereafter, meaning: And do not follow the inclinations of those who do not believe in the Hereafter, so you deny what they deny of God’s reviving His creation after their death, and His resurrection of them after their annihilation, and they equate others with their Lord, meaning: And with their denial of the resurrection after death, and their denial of the coming of the Hour, they equate idols and statues with God, making them equal to Him, and taking them as rivals to Him, worshipping them instead of Him. A group of interpreters said something similar to what we said about this. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Husayn told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement: Bring your witnesses who testify that God has forbidden this, meaning: Say: Show me those who testify that God has forbidden this of what the Arabs have forbidden, and they said, It is a righteous thing that God has commanded us to do. God said to His Messenger: But if they testify, then do not testify with them. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Bring your witnesses who testify that God has forbidden this, he said: The lakes and the seeb.
6:151: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to those who equate idols and statues with their Lord, claiming that God has forbidden them what they have forbidden of their crops and livestock, as I mentioned to you in My revelation to you: Come, O people, I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden, the truth with certainty, not the falsehood of your imagination, your imagination of God is lies and slander, but a revelation from God that He revealed to me, and a revelation that He sent down to me: that you do not associate anything with God from His creation, and do not equate idols and statues with Him, and do not worship anything other than Him, and to parents, good treatment, meaning: And He enjoined good treatment of parents, and He omitted enjoined and commanded, because the speech indicates it and the listener knows its meaning. We have explained that with its evidence in what has come before in the Book. As for the word that in his statement: that you do not associate anything with Him, it is raised, because the meaning of the statement is: Say, Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you, which is that you do not associate anything with Him. If that is what he meant, then in his saying: associate partners, there are two aspects: the jussive mood of prohibition, and directing la to the meaning of prohibition. And the accusative, to direct the speech to the report, and the accusative of associate partners, is an, as one says: I ordered you not to stand. And if you wish, you can put an in the accusative case, in response to what we explained about it, and in his saying: associate partners, there are also two aspects of parsing, similar to what was in it from it. And an is in the nominative case. The interpretation of the statement then would be: Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you. I will recite that you do not associate anything with Him. If someone were to say: How is it possible for His statement: associate to be in the accusative case because of an la, or how is it possible for His statement: that you do not associate to be directed to it, in the sense of report, and He has conjoined it with His statement: And do not kill your children for fear of poverty, and what follows that of the jussive of prohibition? It was said: This is permissible, as God Almighty said: Say, ‘I have been commanded to be the first to submit.’ So He made to be the predicate, and that the noun, then He conjoined it with and do not be among the polytheists. And as the poet said: He went on pilgrimage and ordered Salma Al-Abed not to see or talk to anyone. And her drink remains cold So he made his statement: Do not see a statement, then he connected it with a prohibition and said: Do not speak and Do not slip. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty means by His statement: And do not kill your children for fear of poverty, do not bury your children alive, killing them for fear of poverty due to their expenses, for God is the Provider for you and them. Their provision is not upon you, so you fear for yourselves the inability to provide for their provisions and sustenance. Poverty is a noun derived from the saying of the speaker: I am poor of provisions, so I am poor in poverty, meaning if his provisions are exhausted, his money is gone, and he becomes bankrupt. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And do not kill your children for fear of poverty, poverty is destitution. They killed their children for fear of poverty. Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And do not kill your children for fear of poverty, meaning fear of destitution. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And do not kill your children for fear of poverty, he said: Poverty is destitution. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said, regarding his statement: from poverty, he said: their devils, ordering them to bury their children alive for fear of poverty. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement: from poverty, meaning: from fear of poverty. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: “And do not approach the apparent of the things forbidden to you, which are openly among you and you do not deny doing them, and the hidden of them which you do in secret and do not declare them openly, for all of that is forbidden.” It has been said: It was only said: Do not approach the apparent of the indecencies and what is hidden, because they considered some of the meanings of adultery ugly but not others. What they said about that is not refuted, except that the apparent evidence of the revelation is on the prohibition of the apparent and hidden aspects of every indecency, and there is no report that cuts off the excuse, that it meant some and not all. And it is not permissible to refer the apparent meaning of the Book of God to its hidden meaning, except with an argument that must be accepted. Mention of those who said what we mentioned of those who said: The verse has a specific meaning. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And do not approach immoralities - whether apparent or hidden. As for what is apparent, it is the fornication of shops, and as for what is hidden, it is what is hidden. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding his statement: And do not approach immoralities - whether apparent or concealed, the people of the Age of Ignorance used to conceal their adultery and consider it permissible as long as it was secret. So God forbade both the secret and the public of it. Which of it is apparent means the public, and which is concealed means the secret. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And do not approach immoralities - whether apparent or concealed, he said: In the Age of Ignorance, they did not see anything wrong with fornication in secret, but they considered it ugly in public, so God forbade fornication in secret and in public. Others said the same thing as we said. Who said that? Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And do not approach immoralities - whether apparent or hidden, its secret and its public. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told me, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, something similar. Others said: What is apparent is marriage to mothers and the wives of fathers, and what is hidden is adultery. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid: And do not come near to immoralities - whether apparent or concealed. He said: What is apparent refers to marrying two sisters, or a man marrying his father’s wife after him, and what is concealed refers to adultery. Others said about that as follows: Ishaq bin Ziyad Al-Attar Al-Nasri told me, he said, Muhammad bin Ishaq Al-Balkhi told us, he said, Tamim bin Shakir Al-Bahili told us, on the authority of Isa bin Abi Hafsa, he said: I heard Al-Dahhak say about His statement: And do not approach immoralities - whether apparent or concealed, he said: What is apparent is alcohol, and what is concealed is adultery. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: “Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you: that you not associate anything with Him.” And do not kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right. He means by the soul which God has forbidden to be killed, the soul of a believer or a person with whom a treaty has been made. His statement: except by right, means by what He has permitted its killing: that a person kills a soul and is killed in retaliation for it, or commits adultery while married and is stoned, or apostatizes from her true religion and is killed. This is the right by which God Almighty has permitted the killing of a soul which He has forbidden the believers to kill. That, meaning these matters which our Lord has commanded us not to do and not to abandon, are the matters which He has commanded us and the disbelievers to all act upon. That you may understand, meaning: He has commanded you to do this so that you may understand what your Lord has commanded you to do.
6:152: Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, meant by His saying: And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in a way that is best, is that do not approach his property except in a way that is good for him and makes him fruitful, as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid: And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in a way that is best, he said: Trading in it. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And do not approach the property of an orphan except in a way that is best, so let his money grow. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Fadil bin Marzouq Al-Anzi told us, on the authority of Salit bin Bilal, on the authority of Al-Dahhak bin Muzahim, regarding his statement: And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in a way that is best, he said: He seeks it for him, and does not take anything from his profit. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said about His statement: And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in a way that is best, he said: That which is best, is that he should eat in moderation if he is poor, and if he is rich, he should not eat. God said: And whoever is rich, let him abstain, and whoever is poor, let him eat in moderation. He said: He was asked about clothing, and he said: God did not mention clothing, rather He mentioned eating. As for His statement: until he reaches his full strength, then ashd is the plural of shadd, just as adhar is the plural of darr, and ashr is the plural of shar, and shadd is strength, and it is the consolidation of the strength of one’s youth and age, just as the day is intense in its height and extension. It is said: I came to him at the height of the day, and the length of the day, and that is when it is intense and intense. Al-Mufaddal, as far as I have heard, used to recite a verse from Antarah: I remember him during the day, as if his hair and hair were dyed with honey. And from it the other said: A tall, pure-handed, pure-bred woman walks around him all day long. Some Basrans claimed that the most severe is like the most severe. As for the people of interpretation, they differ on the time when a person reaches it and it is said: he has reached his prime. Some of them said: This is said to him when he reaches puberty. Who said that? Ahmad bin Abdul Rahman told me, he said, my uncle told us, he said, Yahya bin Ayoub told me, on the authority of Amr bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Rabi’a regarding his statement: until he reaches his maturity, he said: the dream. Ahmad bin Abdul Rahman told me, he said, my uncle told us, he said, Abdul Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam told me, on the authority of his father, the same. Ibn Wahb said: Malik told me the same. Al-Hammani narrated that Hisham narrated to us, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Amer: Until he reaches maturity. He said: maturity is patience, when good deeds are recorded for him and bad deeds are recorded against him. Others said: This is only said to him when he reaches the age of thirty. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Until he reaches his maturity, he said: As for his maturity, it is thirty years, then after that came: Until they reach the age of marriage. There is an omission in the speech, which was left out because it was sufficient to indicate what was apparent from what was omitted. That is because the meaning of the speech is: And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in a way that is best, until he reaches maturity. “When he reaches maturity,” and you perceive in him sound judgment, then give him his money, because He, the Most High, did not forbid approaching the property of an orphan while he is an orphan, except in a way that is best, until he reaches maturity, so that it would be permissible for his guardian after he reaches maturity to approach it in a way that is worse. Rather, He forbade them from approaching it out of caution for him and to protect him, so that they would hand it over to him when he reaches maturity. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: “Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you: that you not associate anything with Him,” and that you give full measure and weight. He says: Do not deprive those who are given full measure when you measure them, or full weight when you weigh them, but give them their due rights. Giving them that means giving them their due rights in full, in justice, meaning in fairness, as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: With justice, with fairness. We have explained the meaning of justice with evidence previously, and we dislike repeating it. As for His statement: We do not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity, He is saying: We do not charge a soul, of giving full measure and weight, except what it can bear, so that it is permissible for it and there is no difficulty in it. This is because God, the Most High, knows that many of His servants are too constrained to give others what they are not obligated to do for them, so He commanded the giver to fulfill the right of the Lord of the right that is his, and He did not charge him with more, because more than that would cause his soul to be constrained by it. And He commanded the one who has the right to take his right, and He did not charge him with being satisfied with less than that, because less than that would cause his soul to be constrained. So He did not charge a soul except with what there is no difficulty or difficulty in, and for that reason He said: We do not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. We have already explained this in detail with evidence in a place other than this one, so there is no need to repeat it. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty means by His statement, And when you speak, be just, that if you judge between people and speak, then speak the truth between them, and be just and fair and do not be unjust, even if the one against whom the truth and judgment are directed is a relative of yours. Do not let the kinship of a relative or the friendship of a friend between whom you judge and someone else lead you to say something other than the truth in what he has referred to you for judgment. And fulfill the covenant of God, He says: And fulfill the commandment of God that He has commanded you. Fulfilling that means obeying Him in what He has commanded them to do and what He has forbidden them to do, and acting according to His Book and the Sunnah of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. And that is fulfilling the covenant of God. As for His statement: This is what He has enjoined upon you, the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to those of your people who are just with God, idols and statues: These matters that I have mentioned to you in these two verses are the things that our Lord has enjoined upon us, and your Lord has enjoined upon you, and commanded you to act upon, not with the Baha’ir, the Sa’ib, the Wasa’il, the Ham, killing children, burying girls alive, and following in the footsteps of Satan, so that you may remember. He says: He has enjoined upon you these matters that He has enjoined upon you in these two verses, and enjoined upon you and enjoined upon you in them, so that you may remember the consequences of your actions and the error of what you are doing, so that you may refrain from them, be deterred and turn back to obeying your Lord. Ibn Abbas used to say: These verses are the decisive verses. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Ali bin Saleh, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abdullah bin Qais, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: They are the decisive verses, His statement: Say, ‘Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you - that you not associate anything with Him.’ Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, they said, Wahb ibn Jarir told us, he said, my father told us, he heard Yahya ibn Ayoub narrating, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib, on the authority of Marthad ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Adi ibn al-Khayyar, he said: Ka’b al-Ahbar heard a man reciting: Say, ‘Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you.’ So he said: By the One in Whose Hand is Ka’b’s soul, this is the first thing in the Torah: Say, ‘Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you.’ Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Saeed bin Masrouq, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ar-Rabi’ bin Khaitham: that he said to a man: Do you want a scroll with the seal of Muhammad on it? Then he recited these verses: Say, Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you - that you not associate anything with Him. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ishaq Al-Razi told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, he said: Al-Rabi’ said: Shall I not read to you a document from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? He did not say: Its seal. So he recited these verses: “Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you.” Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, he said: A group of people came to him and said: You have sat with the companions of Muhammad, so tell us about the revelation. He recited to them these verses from al-An’am 6:Say, 'Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you - that you not associate anything with Him.' They said, We do not ask you about this. He said, We have no revelation other than this. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said: These are the verses that he recommended from the decisive Qur’an. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement: And when you speak, be just, he said: Speak the truth.
6:153: Abu Ja`far said: The Almighty says: This is what your Lord has commanded you, O people, in these two verses of His saying: “Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you,” and He has commanded you to fulfill it, it is His path, meaning: His way and religion that He has chosen for His servants, straight, meaning: upright, with no deviation from the truth, so follow it, meaning: so act upon it, and make it a path for yourselves that you follow, so follow it, and do not follow other paths, meaning: do not follow a path other than it, and do not adopt a method other than it, and do not seek a religion contrary to it, from Judaism, Christianity, Zoroastrianism, idolatry, and other religions, for they are innovations and misguidance, for it will separate you from His way, meaning, it will disperse you, if you follow the newly invented paths that are not paths, ways, or religions for God, your following It, by His way, meaning: by His path and religion that He has prescribed for you and that He has chosen, which is Islam, which He has commanded the prophets to follow and which He has commanded the nations before you to follow. That is what He has commanded you to do, the Most High says: This is what your Lord has commanded you to do, by His saying to you: Indeed, this is My path, which is straight, so follow it and do not follow [other] ways, He has commanded you to do it that you may become righteous, meaning: So that you may fear God in yourselves and not destroy them, and beware of your Lord in them and not anger Him with them, lest His vengeance and punishment befall you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: And do not follow other paths, for they will separate you from His path, he said: Innovations and doubts. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Shibl, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said it. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayj, on the authority of Mujahid: And do not follow the paths, innovations and doubts. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: So follow him and do not follow other paths, for they will separate you from His path, and his statement: Establish the religion and do not be divided therein, and something similar to this is in the Qur’an. He said: God commanded the believers to remain in congregation, and forbade them from disagreement and division, and informed them that those who came before them were destroyed only by arguments and disputes over the religion of God. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And do not follow paths, for they will separate you from His path, meaning: Do not follow misguidance. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abi Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah, he said, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, drew a line for us one day and said, ‘This is the path of God.’ Then he drew lines to the right and left of that line and said, ‘These are paths, on each path of which is a devil calling to it.’ Then he recited this verse: ‘And indeed, this is My path, which is straight, so follow it and do not follow [other] paths, for they will separate you from His path.’” Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And that this is My path, which is straight, so follow it and do not follow [other] paths, for they will separate you from His path, he said: His path is Islam, and His path is Islam. He forbade them from following paths other than His, for they will separate you from His path, from Islam. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told me, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Abaan: That a man said to Ibn Mas'ud: What is the straight path? He said: We left Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, at its lowest point, and its edge is in Paradise, and on his right is a horse and on his left is a horse, and there are men calling whoever passes by them. Whoever takes that horse will end up in the Fire, and whoever takes the path will end up in Paradise. Then Ibn Mas'ud recited: And that this is My straight path, the verse. Abu Jaafar said: There are different readings of the verse: And that this is My straight path. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra and some of the Kufians read it as: And with the alif of an open and the nun doubled, in response to his statement: That you should not associate anything with Him, meaning: “Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you: that you should not associate anything with Him,” that this is My straight path. The majority of the Kufians read it as: T N with the alif of an open and the nun doubled, as a beginning and a break from the first, since the speech had ended with the report of the commandment that God commanded His servants to do, without Him, according to them. Abu Jaafar said: The correct statement regarding this, in my opinion, is that they are two widely used readings in the readings of the regions and the common Muslims, and their meanings are correct. The remaining two readings are read by the reader, so he is correct in his reading. And that is because God, the Most High, has commanded following His path, just as He commanded His prophets to His servants, even if that is included in what God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say to the polytheists: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you, and what He commanded you to do, and so He opened up to that, so he is correct, because he broke it, since the recitation was a statement, and if it was not in the wording of the statement because of its distance from His saying: I will not recite, and He wants to apply that to it, so he is correct, and if he broke it in the sense of beginning and stopping from the first and the recitation and that what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded to be recited to those who were commanded to recite it to them ended before that, so he is correct. Abdullah bin Abi Ishaq Al-Basri read it as: And with the opening of the alif of an and the softening of the nun of it, meaning: “Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you - that you not associate anything with Him” and that this is My path. So he softened it, since the an in His statement: that you not associate anything with Him was softened, and the an of His statement: that this is My path was conjoined to it, so he made it similar to what it was conjoined to. And even though this is a doctrine, I do not like the reading with it, because it is an anomaly from the reading of the reading of the regions, and contrary to what they are upon in their regions.
6:154: Abu Ja'far said: What God, the Most High, meant by His statement: Then We gave Moses the Scripture, then say after that, O Muhammad: Your Lord gave Moses the Scripture. So He left out mentioning Say, since what had been mentioned at the beginning of the story indicated that it was intended in it, and that is His statement: "Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you," so He narrated what He prohibited to them and permitted, then He said: Then say: We gave Moses, so He omitted Say because His statement Say indicated it to him, and that it was intended in the speech. And we only said: That was intended in the speech, because Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was undoubtedly sent after Moses by a long time, and that he was only commanded to recite these verses to those who were commanded to recite them to him after his mission. And it is known that Moses was given the Scripture before God commanded Muhammad to recite these verses to those who were commanded to recite them to him. And Then, in the speech of the Arabs, is a letter that indicates that what comes after it of speech and report comes after what came before it. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of his saying: Completely upon the one who does good. Some of them said: Its meaning is: Completely upon the doers of good. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Completely upon the one who does good, the believers and the doers of good. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Completely upon the one who does good, the believers and the doers of good. And Mujahid directed the interpretation of the words and their meaning to the fact that God, may He be glorified, informed about Moses that He gave him the Book as a virtue over what He gave to the righteous among His servants. If someone were to say: How is it permissible to say: upon the one who did good, making upon the one who singular, and the interpretation upon those who did good? It would be said: The Arabs do that especially with upon the one who and with the definite article, if they mean all and everyone, as God Almighty said: By time, indeed, mankind is in loss, and as they said: The dirham has become abundant in the hands of the people. It was mentioned on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud that he used to recite it: Completely for those who do good. This is from his recitation in this way, which supports the statement of Mujahid. If the meaning is thus, then his saying do good is a past tense verb, and so its accusative is for this reason. It may be permissible for do good to be in the genitive case, but it is accusative since af’al and af’al do not apply to their speech. If it is said: Then by what is it in the genitive case? It was said: In response to who, since he did not see what would raise it, so the interpretation of the speech then would be: Then We gave Moses the Book, completing it for what is best, then he deleted who, and who is best was placed next to who, so it was Arabized according to its Arabization, since it was like the definite article, because the definite article does not enter it, and who is like it, as the Arabs say: I passed by the one who is better than you, and worse than you, as the rajaz poet said: Al-Zubaidi, who represented the dream, was named after you, people of knowledge. Follow the example of the one who, in grammar. Whoever said that did not say: I passed by the one who knows, because the one who knows is indefinite and the one who is definite, and an indefinite does not follow a definite. Others said: The meaning of that is: Completely upon the one who did good, Moses, in what God tested him with in this world of His commands and prohibitions. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’: Then We gave Moses the Scripture, completing it for him who did good, in what God gave him. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Then We gave Moses the Scripture, completing it for him who did good. He said: Whoever does good in this world, God will complete that for him in the Hereafter. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his saying: Then We gave Moses the Scripture, perfecting it for him who did good, meaning: whoever did good in this world, God’s honor will be completed for him in the Hereafter. According to this interpretation, which Al-Rabi’ interpreted, ahsan is in the accusative case, because it is a past tense verb, and alladhi means what, and the speech at that time was: Then We gave Moses the Scripture, complete for what Moses did well, meaning: We gave him the Scripture to complete for him My honor in the Hereafter, complete for his goodness in this world in worshipping God and doing what He charged him with in obeying Him. Others said about that: Its meaning is: Then We gave Moses the Scripture, complete for what God did well to His prophets and His favors to them. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said about His statement, Then We gave Moses the Scripture, complete for him who did good, he said: Complete from God for His goodness to them and His guidance to Islam, and He gave them that Scripture, complete, for His favor and goodness upon them. And did good according to this interpretation also, is in the accusative case, as a past tense verb, and which according to this statement and the statement that al-Rabi’ said, means: what. It was mentioned from Yahya ibn Ya’mar that he used to read that: Complete for him who did good, in the nominative case, with the interpretation of on the one who is better. Ahmad bin Yusuf told me that, he said, Al-Qasim bin Salam told us, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Abu Amr bin Al-Ala, on the authority of Yahya bin Ya’mar. Abu Jaafar said: This is a reading that I do not permit reading, because it has a correct meaning in Arabic, because it contradicts what is agreed upon by the evidence from the readings of the regions. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of these sayings, in my opinion, is the saying of the one who said that its meaning is: Then We gave Moses the Book, completing Our favors to him, upon the one who did well by Moses in fulfilling Our commands and prohibitions, because that is the most apparent meaning in the speech, and that giving Moses his book was a blessing from God upon him and a great favor. So He, the Most High, informed us that He bestowed that blessing upon him because of his previous righteous deeds and good obedience. If the interpretation was as Ibn Zayd said, the statement would be: Then We gave Moses the Scripture, completing what we did well, or: Then God gave Moses the Scripture, completing what we did well. And in His description of Himself, may His praise be glorified, as giving Him the Scripture, then diverting the report by saying: He did well to someone other than the one informing about Himself, by the closeness between the two report items, there is clear evidence that the statement is not the statement that Ibn Zayd said. As for what was mentioned about Mujahid directing who to mean everyone, there is no evidence in the speech indicating the correctness of what he said about that, rather the apparent meaning of the speech is more similar to what we have chosen from the statement. And if there is division in the interpretation of the speech, the most appropriate meaning for it is the one that is most likely to be based on the apparent meaning, unless there is clear evidence from reason or report that it means something other than that. As for his saying: And a detailed explanation of everything, he means: And a clarification of everything from the matter of the religion that they were commanded to do. The interpretation of the statement is: Then We gave Moses the Torah to complete Our favors to him and Our favors before him, by which Our honor was completed for him for his kindness and obedience to his Lord and his fulfillment of what He commanded him of the laws of His religion, and to clarify everything that his people and followers needed of their religious affairs, as Bishr told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And a detailed explanation of everything, in it is its lawful and unlawful. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: We gave Moses the Book, complete and detailed for everything, and guidance, meaning by His saying: and guidance, setting them on the straight path, and explaining to them the paths of guidance so that they do not go astray, and mercy, meaning: and mercy from Us to them and compassion, to save them from misguidance and the blindness of confusion. As for his saying: Perhaps they will believe in the meeting with their Lord, it means: My giving Moses the Book to complete God’s honor to Moses, for the goodness of Moses, and to detail the laws of His religion, and guidance for those who followed him, and mercy for those among them who were astray, so that God would save them from misguidance, and so that they would believe in the meeting with their Lord if they heard God’s admonitions with which He admonished His creation in Him, so that they would be deterred from what they were upon, of disbelief in Him and in the meeting with Him after his death, so that they would obey their Lord and believe in what His Prophet Moses, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought to them.
6:155: Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, meant by His saying: And this is a blessed Book which We have sent down, is this Qur’an which We sent down to our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. A blessed Book which We have sent down, so follow it, meaning: So make it an imam whom you follow and act according to what is in it, O people. And fear God, meaning: And beware of God in yourselves, lest you neglect to act according to what is in it, transgress its limits, and make permissible what is forbidden by it, as: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And this is a blessed Book which We have revealed, which is the Qur’an that God revealed to Muhammad, peace be upon him, so follow it, meaning: follow what He has made lawful and forbid what He has forbidden. And His saying: Perhaps you will have mercy, means: So that you may have mercy, and be saved from the punishment of God and His painful chastisement.
6:156: Abu Ja`far said: The Arab scholars differed regarding the factor of an in His statement: that you say and regarding the meaning of this statement. Some of the Nahim of Basra said: The meaning of this is: Then We gave Moses the Book, completing it for him who did good, out of dislike for you to say: The Book was only sent down to two groups before us. Some of the people of Kufa said: Rather, it is in the accusative case with an implied verb. He said: The meaning of the statement is: So follow him and fear God, that you may receive mercy. Fear God lest you say. He said: And similarly, God says: That your deeds may become worthless while you perceive not. Others among them said: It is in the accusative case. He said: Its accusative case is from two places: One of them is: We sent it down so that they would not say, The Book was only sent down to two groups before us, and the other is from His statement: Beware. He said: It is not appropriate in the place of that like His statement: God makes clear to you, lest you go astray. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of these sayings, in my opinion, is the saying of the one who said: An is in the accusative case because it is related to the revelation, because the meaning of the statement is: “This is a blessed book that We have revealed, so that you will not say: ‘The Book was only revealed to two groups before us.’” As for the two groups that God mentioned, and He informed us that He only sent down His Book to His Prophet Muhammad so that the polytheists would not say: No book was sent down to us so that we could follow it, and we were not commanded or forbidden, then there is no proof against us in what we do and leave, since no book or messenger came to us from God. Rather, the proof is against the two groups to whom the Book was sent down before us, and they are the Jews and the Christians, and the people of interpretation said the same. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: That you should not say, ‘The Book was only sent down to two groups before us,’ and they are the Jews and the Christians. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: That you may say, ‘The Book was only sent down to two groups before us,’ the Jews and the Christians. He feared that the Quraysh would say it. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: That you say, ‘The Book was only revealed to two groups before us,’ he said: The Jews and the Christians. He said: That you say, Quraysh. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: That you say, ‘The Book was only sent down to two groups before us,’ and they are the Jews and the Christians. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: The Book was only revealed to two groups before us, as for the two groups, they are the Jews and the Christians. As for And if we were unaware of their study, it means: that you say: And we were unaware of the recitation of the two groups of the Book that was sent down to them, we do not know what it is, nor do we know what they read or say, nor what was sent down to them in their Book, because they were its people and not us, and we were not concerned with it nor were we commanded to do what is in it, nor is it in our language, so they take that as an argument. So God cut off their argument by sending down the Qur’an to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And we were heedless of their study, meaning: And we were heedless of their recitation. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And we were unaware of their study, meaning: of their reading. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And if we were unaware of their study, he said, study means reading and knowledge. And he read: And they studied what was in it. He said: They knew what was in it, they did not come to it in ignorance. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And if we were unaware of their study, he says: And if we were unaware of their reading, we do not know what it is.
6:157: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: And this is a blessed Book which We have sent down, so that the polytheists among the idolaters of Quraysh would not say: The Book was sent down to two groups before us, or: so that they would not say: If the Book had been sent down to us as it was sent down to these two groups before us, and He had commanded us in it and forbidden us, and explained to us in it the error of what we are in from its correctness, we would have been better guided than them, meaning: we would have been more upright on the path of truth, and more following of the Book, and better in doing what is in it, than the two groups to whom the Book was sent down before us. God says: There has come to you a clear proof from your Lord, meaning: There has come to you a Book in your language, clear Arabic, a clear argument against you, clear and evident from your Lord, and guidance, meaning: and an explanation of the truth, and a distinction between right and wrong, and mercy for those who act upon it and follow it, as: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Or you should say, ‘If only the Scripture had been sent down to us, we would have been better guided than they.’ But there has come to you clear evidence from your Lord. He says: Clear evidence has come to you, a clear Arabic language, when you did not know the study of the two groups, and when you said, ‘If only a Scripture had come to us, we would have been better guided than them.’ But there has come to you clear evidence from your Lord.” Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Or you say, ‘If only the Scripture had been sent down to us, we would have been better guided than they are.’ This is what the Arab infidels said, But there has come to you clear evidence from your Lord and guidance and mercy. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: So whoever has committed an act of error and is more aggressive than you, O polytheists who deny God’s proofs and evidence - which are His signs - and turned away from them, meaning: and turned away from them after they came to him, so he did not believe in them, and did not believe in their truth. And He, the Most High, brought out the report by saying: Who is more unjust than he who denies the signs of God? Bringing out the report about the absent person, and what is meant by it are the polytheists of Quraysh who were addressed by it. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of his statement: And he turned away from it, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And he turned away from it, meaning: he turned away from it. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: They turn away from Our signs, they turn away from them, and turning away means turning away. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And he turned away from it, he turned away from it, We will reward those who turn away from Our signs with a terrible punishment for what they used to turn away, meaning: they turned away. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: And turned away from it, meaning he turned away from it. And His statement, We will reward those who turn away from Our signs with an evil punishment, means: God will reward those who turn away from His signs and proofs and do not ponder them, and do not recognize their reality and believe in what they have shown them of the Oneness of God, and the reality of the Prophethood of His Prophet, and the truth of what he brought to them from their Lord, an evil punishment, means: severe punishment, and that is the punishment of the Fire that God has prepared for the disbelievers in His creation, because they turned away, means: God will do that to them as a punishment for what they turned away from His signs in this world, and they did not accept what their Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought to them.
6:158: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Do these people who are just with their Lord await idols and statues, except that the angels come to them, with death and take their souls, or that your Lord, O Muhammad, comes to them among His creation in the place of resurrection, or that some of the signs of your Lord come, meaning: or that some of the signs of your Lord come to them. And that is, according to what the people of interpretation said: the rising of the sun from the west. Those who interpreted this said: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Unless the angels come to them, he said: at death when they die, or your Lord comes, that is on the Day of Resurrection, or some of the signs of your Lord come, the rising of the sun from the west. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Unless the angels come to them, with death, or your Lord comes, on the Day of Resurrection, or some of the signs of your Lord come, he said: A positive sign, the rising of the sun from the west, or whatever God wills. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them, he said: with death, or that your Lord should come, and that is on the Day of Resurrection, or that some of the signs of your Lord should come. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them, at death, or that your Lord should come, or that some of the signs of your Lord should come, he said: the rising of the sun from the west.
