Ibn Wakee’ and Ibn Hameed told us, they said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Ad-Dahha, on the authority of Masruq, he said, Abdullah said regarding His statement, Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them or your Lord should come or some of the signs of your Lord should come? He said: They will wake up and the sun and moon will be from here towards the west, like two camels paired together. Ibn Hameed added in his hadeeth: That is when faith will not benefit a soul if it did not believe before or earn any good through its faith, and he said: like two camels paired together. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement: Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them, seizing the souls by death, or that your Lord should come, on the Day of Resurrection, or that some of the signs of your Lord should come? Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says: On the Day when some of the signs of your Lord come, it will not benefit someone who was previously a polytheist to God to believe after the coming of that sign. It was said: That verse in which God Almighty informed that the faith of the unbeliever will not benefit him when it comes: the rising of the sun from the west. Mention who said that, and what was mentioned about it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Isa bin Othman Al-Ramli told me, he said, Yahya bin Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Atiyah, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: On the Day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith, he said: The rising of the sun from the west. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Atiyah, on the authority of Abu Saeed, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the same. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Fadil and Jarir told us, on the authority of Amara, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Hour will not come until the sun rises from the West. He said: So when the people see it, those who are on it will believe, and that is when ‘faith will not benefit a soul if it did not believe before or earn good through its faith.’ Abdul Hamid bin Bayan Al-Sakari and Ishaq bin Shaheen narrated to us, they said: Khalid bin Abdullah Al-Tahan informed us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taimi, on the authority of his father, “On the authority of Abu Dharr, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said one day: Do you know where this sun goes? They said: God and His Messenger know best! He said: It goes to its resting place under the Throne, then falls prostrate, and remains like that until it is told: Rise from wherever you wish, so it rises from its rising place. Then it runs until it reaches its resting place under the Throne, then falls prostrate, and remains like that until it is told: Rise from wherever you wish, so it rises from its rising place. Then it runs, and people do not object to anything about it, until it reaches its resting place under the Throne, and people do not object to anything about it, so it is told: Rise from your setting place, so it rises from its setting place. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you know what day that is? They said: God and His Messenger know best! He said: That is the day “No soul will benefit from its faith if it does not rise from its setting place.” She had not believed before or gained any good through her faith.” Muammil bin Hisham and Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, they said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Yazid al-Taymi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Dharr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ubayd God told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Safwan ibn Assal, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told us: “Before the setting of the sun, there is an open door for repentance until the sun rises from its direction. But when the sun rises from its direction, faith will not benefit a soul that did not believe before or earn good through its faith.” Al-Mufaddal bin Ishaq told us, he said, Ash’ath bin Abd al-Rahman bin Zubayd al-Ayami told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Zubayd, on the authority of Zur bin Hubaish, on the authority of Safwan bin Assal al-Muradi, he said: I mentioned repentance, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is a gate to repentance in the west, a distance of seventy years - or: forty years - and it will remain like that until some of the signs of your Lord come. Muhammad bin Amara told me, he said, Sahl bin Aamer told us, he said, Malik told us, on the authority of Asim bin Abi Al-Najoud, on the authority of Zur bin Hubaish, on the authority of Safwan bin Assal, that he said: In the West there is an open door to repentance, a distance of seventy years. When the sun rises from the West, no soul will benefit from its faith if it did not believe before or gain good through its faith. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Ammarah ibn al-Qa’qa’, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah, “On the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The Hour will not come until the sun rises from the West. When it rises and the people see it, those who are on it will believe, and that will be the time when ‘faith will not benefit a soul if it did not believe before.’” Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Khalid bin Mukhallad told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ja`far told us, on the authority of Al-`Ala`, on the authority of his father, “on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Hour will not come until the sun sets from the West, and on that day all people will believe together, and that will be when “no soul will benefit from its faith if it did not believe before or earn any good through its faith.” Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, “On the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: Repentance is accepted, as long as the sun does not rise from the west.” Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Tirmidhi told us, Sulayman ibn Abd al-Rahman told us, Ibn Ayyash told us, Damdam ibn Zur’ah told us, on the authority of Shureih ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Malik ibn Yakhamir, on the authority of Mu’awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, and Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-’As, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Repentance will continue to be accepted until the sun rises from the West. When it rises, every heart will be sealed with what is in it, and people will be spared the burden of deeds.” Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Abu Usama and Jaafar bin Awn told us, something similar. Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Hayyan al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah, who said: Three Muslims sat with Marwan ibn al-Hakam in Medina, and they heard him talking about the signs: The first of them will be the emergence of the Antichrist. The people turned to Abdullah ibn Amr and told him about that, and he said: Marwan did not say anything! I have memorized something from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that which I have not forgotten. I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The first of the signs to emerge will be the rising of the sun from the west, or the emergence of the beast among the people at noon. Whichever of the two comes first, the other will follow soon after it. Then Abdullah bin Amr, who used to read the books, said: I think the first of them to emerge is the rising of the sun from the west. That is because whenever it sets, it comes under the Throne, prostrates, and asks permission to return, and permission is given to it to return. Then, when it appears to God that it should rise from the west, it does as it used to do. It comes under the Throne, prostrates, and asks permission to return, but He does not respond to it at all. So it does that three times, and He does not respond to it at all. Then, when what God willed of the night has passed, and it knows that if He gave it permission, it would not reach the east, it says: How far is the east! My Lord, who will help me with the people? Until, when the horizon becomes like a necklace, it asks permission to return, and it is said to it: Go up from your place, so it goes up from the west. Then he recited: The Day some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith, to the end of the verse. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Rabia Fahd told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed Abi Hayyan, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi: That three men entered upon Marwan bin Al-Hakam, and he mentioned something similar, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, he said: I heard Asim bin Abi al-Najud, narrating on the authority of Zur bin Hubaish, on the authority of Safwan bin Assal, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: In the West there is a door open to repentance, a distance of seventy years, which will not be closed until the sun rises from its direction. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur ibn Hubaish, on the authority of Safwan ibn Assal, who said: When the sun rises from the West, then on that Day faith will not benefit a soul that did not believe before. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Rabia Fahd told us, he said, Asim bin Bahdalah told us, on the authority of Zur bin Hubaish, he said: I went out in the morning to Safwan bin Assal, and he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The door of repentance is open from the west, its width is the distance of a seventy-year journey, and it will remain open until the sun rises from it. Then he recited: ‘Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them or your Lord should come or some of the signs of your Lord should come? ’ until ‘good. ’” Al-Rabi’ bin Sulayman told me, he said, Shu’ayb bin Al-Layth told us, he said, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Ja’far bin Rabi’ah, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Harmaz: that he said: Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Hour will not come until the sun rises from the west. He said: When the sun rises from the west, all people will believe, and that will be when “Faith will not benefit a soul if it did not believe before or earned any good through its faith. Say, ‘Wait, we are waiting.’” Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever repents before the sun rises from the West, it will be accepted from him. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Fahd told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Yunus bin Ubaid, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Yazid al-Taimi, on the authority of Abu Dharr: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the sun sets, it comes under the Throne and prostrates, and it is said to it: Rise from where it set. Then he recited this verse: ‘Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them?’ to the end of the verse.” Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Sufyan bin Husayn, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taymi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: “I was riding behind the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, one day on a donkey, and he looked at the sun when it set and said: It sets in a hot spring, and it sets until it prostrates before its Lord under the Throne, until He gives it permission. Then when He wants it to rise from its setting place, He stops it, and it says: O Lord, my journey is far. Then He says to it: Rise from where it sets! That is when ‘faith will not benefit a soul if it did not believe before.’” Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abda told us, on the authority of Musa ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Taymi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked one day at the sun and said: It is about to come until it stands before God, and He will say: Go back from where you came! At that time: ‘Faith will not benefit a soul if it did not believe before or earn good through its faith.’” Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying: On the Day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it did not believe before or earned good through its faith, meaning that the faith of a polytheist will not benefit him when the signs are revealed, but it will benefit the people of faith when the signs are revealed if they earned good before that. Ibn Abbas said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out one evening and said to them: O servants of God, repent to God, for you are about to see the sun from the west. When it does that, repentance will be withheld, deeds will be folded up, and faith will be sealed. The people said: Is there a sign for that, O Messenger of God? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The sign of that night is that it will be as long as three nights, and those who fear their Lord will wake up and pray to Him, then they will complete their prayers while the night is still in its place, then they will go to their beds and sleep. Then when they wake up and the night is still in its place, when they see that, they will fear that there is a great matter ahead of them. Then when they wake up and the sun has risen long for them, while they are waiting for it, it will rise from the west. When it does that, no soul will benefit from its faith if it did not believe before.” Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Salih, the freed slave of Al-Taw’amah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah: that he heard him say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Hour will not come until the sun rises from the West. When it rises and the people see it, they will all believe together. On that day, ‘No soul will benefit from its faith,’ the verse.” And he said, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn Abi Atiq told me, that he allowed Ubayd ibn Umair to recite: On the Day some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith, he said, he said: We used to say, and God knows best, that it is the sun rising from the west. Ibn Jurayj said, and Amr ibn Dinar told me: that he heard Ubayd ibn Umair say that. Ibn Jurayj said, and Abdullah ibn Abi Malekah told me: as if he heard Abdullah ibn Amr say: The sign from which faith will not benefit a soul is when the sun rises from the west. Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid also said that. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Zararah ibn Awfa, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud: On the Day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith, he said: The rising of the sun from the west. Muhammad ibn Bashar and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, they said, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, he said, I heard Qatada narrating, on the authority of Zurarah ibn Awfa, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas`ud, regarding this verse: On the Day some of the signs of your Lord come, he said: The rising of the sun from the west. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday and Abdul Wahhab told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, he said, Abu Ubaidah bin Abdullah bin Masoud told me, he said: Abdullah bin Masoud used to say: What was mentioned of the signs have passed except for four: the rising of the sun from the west, the beast of the earth, the Antichrist, the emergence of Gog and Magog, and the sign with which deeds are concluded: the rising of the sun from the west. Have you not seen that God said: The Day some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it did not believe before or earned good through its faith, he said: So it is the rising of the sun from the west. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu`bah, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, he said: Abdullah said: On the Day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith, he said: The rising of the sun from the west with the moon, as if they were two camels tethered together. Shu`bah said, and Qatada told us, on the authority of Zurarah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas`ud: On the Day when some of the signs of your Lord come, he said: The rising of the sun from the west. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud: On the Day when some of the signs of your Lord come, he said: The rising of the sun from the west with the moon, like two camels linked together. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur and Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah: On the Day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith, he said: The rising of the sun from the west with the moon, like two camels together. He said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, and his father, on the authority of Ash’ath bin Abi Al-Sha’tha’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: Repentance is extended as long as the sun does not rise from the west. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: It was mentioned to us that Ibn Umm Abd used to say: The door of repentance will remain open until the sun rises from the West. When people see that, they will believe, and that is when faith will not benefit a soul if it did not believe before or earn any good through its faith. Bishr told us, he said, Abdullah bin Jaafar told us, he said, Al-Ala bin Abdul Rahman told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Hour will not come until the sun rises from the West. When it rises, all people will believe, and on that day, ‘no soul will benefit from its faith if it did not believe before or earn any good through its faith.’” Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ubayd ibn Umair: On the Day when some of the signs of your Lord come, he said: The rising of the sun from the west. He said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Uqbah, Abu Kiran, on the authority of Al-Dahhak: On the Day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith, he said: The rising of the sun from the west. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Israel told us, he said: Ash’ath bin Abi al-Sha’tha’ told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, regarding his statement: Faith will not benefit a soul if it did not believe before, he said: Repentance will continue to be granted as long as the sun does not rise from the west. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: On the Day when some of the signs of your Lord come, he said: The rising of the sun from the west. Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Abu Sakhr told me, on the authority of Al-Qurazi: that he used to say about this verse: On the Day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it did not believe before, he said: When the signs come, no soul will benefit from its faith. He said: The rising of the sun from the west. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Asim bin Abi al-Najud, on the authority of Zur bin Hubaish, on the authority of Safwan bin Ashal: On the Day when some of the signs of your Lord come, he said: The rising of the sun from the west. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Wahb bin Jaber, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr: On the Day when some of the signs of your Lord come, he said: The rising of the sun from the west. Others said: Rather, these are some of the three signs: the beast, Gog and Magog, and the rising of the sun from the west. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ja’far ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Al-Mas’udi, on the authority of Al-Qasim, he said, Abdullah said: Repentance is offered to the son of Adam if he accepts it, as long as one of three things does not happen: the sun rises from the west, the beast, or Gog and Magog are conquered. Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Al-Mas’udi told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abd Al-Rahman, he said: Abdullah said: Repentance is offered to the son of Adam if he accepts it, as long as one of three things does not come out: the beast, the rising of the sun from the west, and the emergence of Gog and Magog. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Aisha, she said: When the first signs come out, the pens will be thrown away, the recorders will be held back, and the bodies will bear witness to the deeds. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are three things that, when they emerge, will not benefit a soul from its faith if it did not believe before or earn any good through its faith: the rising of the sun from the west, the Antichrist, and the beast of the earth.” Bishr bin Muadh told us: Muawiyah bin Abdul Karim told us: Al-Hasan told us: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Hasten to do good deeds before six things happen: the rising of the sun from the west, the Antichrist, the smoke, the beast of the earth, the privy of one of you, and the affairs of the people.” Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: It was mentioned that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say, and he mentioned something similar to it. Abu Jaafar said: The most correct of the sayings on this matter is what the hadiths have agreed upon, “On the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: That is when the sun rises from the west.” As for his saying: or earned good in her faith, it means: or did good in her belief in God, from righteous deeds that confirm and fulfill his words, before the sun rises from the west. And the faith of a disbeliever who did not believe in God before it rises likewise, if he believes and believes in God and His messengers, will not benefit him, because it is a state that does not prevent a sinner from acknowledging God, due to the great terror that will befall them from God’s command. So the ruling on their faith is like the ruling on their faith when the Hour comes, and that is a state in which the dead people will not be prevented from acknowledging the Oneness of God, because they will witness the terrors of that Day that will remove their need for thought, reasoning, research, and consideration. And the one who believed in God and His messengers, and neglected the obligations of God, and did not acquire obedience to God with his limbs, will not benefit from his deeds if he did, and his earnings if he acquired, because of his negligence that preceded before it rose in that, as: Muhammad bin Al-Husayn told me, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: The Day some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it did not believe before or earned good through its faith, meaning it earned good through its belief, righteous deeds. So it is the highest of the people of the Qiblah. If it believed and did not do good before that, then it did after seeing the sign, it will not be accepted from it. If it did good before the sign, then it did good after the sign, it will be accepted from it. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement: On the Day some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith, he said: Whoever is aware of some of the signs while he is doing righteous deeds along with his faith, God will accept his deeds after the verse is revealed, just as He accepted them before that. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to those who treat their Lord as equals with idols and statues: Wait for the angels to come to you with death and take your souls, or for your Lord to come to decide the judgment between us and you on the Day of Resurrection, or for the sun to rise from the west and the records of deeds to be folded, and your faith will not benefit you at that time if you believe, until you know then who among us is right from who is wrong, and the wrongdoer from the good, and the truthful from the liar, and you will know at that time who will be subject to God’s punishment and painful chastisement, and who among us and you will be saved and who will perish - we are waiting for that, so that God may reward us abundantly for our obedience to Him, and our sincerity in worshipping Him, and our singling Him out as Lord over all others, and He will decide between us and you with the truth, and He is the best of judges.
6:159: Abu Jaafar said: The reciters differed in the recitation of his saying: They separated. It was narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar: that Ali, may God be pleased with him, recited: Indeed, those who have divided their religion. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, he said, Hamza Al-Zayyat said: Ali, may God be pleased with him, read it: They divided their religion. He said, Al-Hasan bin Ali told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Qatada: They divided their religion. It seems that Ali went with his saying: They divided their religion, they went out and turned away from it, from separation. And Abdullah bin Masoud read that, as: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Rafe’ told us, on the authority of Zuhair, he said, Abu Ishaq told us: Abdullah used to recite it: They divided their religion. And on this reading - I mean the reading of Abdullah - the reading of Medina, Basra and most of the readers of Kufa. And it is as if Abdullah said with his reading that: that the religion of God is one, and it is the religion of Abraham, the pure, Muslim religion, and that divided the Jews and Christians, so some people became Jews and others became modernists, and they made them into scattered sects. Abu Ja`far said: The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings, each of which has been read by the imams of the recitations, and they are in agreement in meaning and not different. This is because every one who goes astray has departed from his religion, and the parties divided the religion of God which He has chosen for His servants, so some became Jews and others Christians, and some became Zoroastrians. This is the division itself, and the fate of its people is scattered sects, not united. They are separated from the true religion of God, and they are separated from it. So whichever of these the reciter recites, he is correct in his recitation, but I choose the recitation with the greatest recitation, which is the emphasis on the ra’ from faraqu. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the two meanings of his saying: Indeed, those who divided their religion. Some of them said: He meant the Jews and Christians. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: And they were sects, he said: Jews. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: They divided their religion, he said: They are the Jews and Christians. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects, of the Jews and Christians. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Those who divided their religion and became sects, you are not from them in anything, these are the Jews and Christians. As for his saying: divided their religion, he says: they abandoned their religion and became sects. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects, that is because the Jews and Christians differed before Muhammad was sent, so they split up. Then when Muhammad was sent, God revealed: Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects - you are not of them in anything. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects, meaning the Jews and Christians. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hussain bin Ali told us, on the authority of Shaiban, on the authority of Qatada: They divided their religion, he said: They are the Jews and Christians. Others said: He meant by that the people of innovation from this nation, who followed the ambiguous verses of the Qur’an rather than the clear verses. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: Indeed, those who have divided their religion, he said: This verse was revealed about this nation. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Abu Hurairah: Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects, he said: They are the people of prayer. Saeed bin Amr Al-Sakuni told me, he said, Baqiyah bin Al-Waleed told us, he said: He wrote to Ibad bin Katheer, he said, Laith told me, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, regarding this verse: Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects - you are not of them in anything, and they are not from you, they are the people of innovations, the people of doubts, and the people of misguidance, from this nation. Abu Ja`far said: The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that God informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that He is innocent of those who left His true religion and divided it, and they were sects and parties in it, and that he is not from them, nor are they from him, because the religion with which God sent him is Islam, the religion of Abraham, the upright one, as his Lord said to him and commanded him to say: Say, ‘Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a right religion, the religion of Abraham, the upright one, and he was not of the polytheists.’ Whoever left the religion with which he was sent, may God bless him and grant him peace, whether a polytheist, a Jew, a Christian, or a monotheist, is an innovator who has innovated in the religion what led him astray from the straight path and the true religion, the religion of Abraham the Muslim. He is innocent of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Muhammad is innocent of him. He is included in the generality of his statement: Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects - you are not of them in anything. As for his saying: “You are not of them in anything. Their affair is with God,” the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: This verse was revealed to the Prophet of God with the command to stop fighting the polytheists before the obligation of fighting them became obligatory, then it was abrogated by the command to fight them in Surat Bara’ah, and that is His saying: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, his saying: “You are not of them in anything. Their affair is only with God,” he was not commanded to fight them, then we became angry, so he was commanded to fight them in Surat Al-Bara’ah. Others said: Rather, it was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as an announcement from God to him that there would be among his nation those who would innovate in his religion after him. It is not abrogated, because it is a report, not a command, and abrogation only occurs in commands and prohibitions. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said, Malik bin Mughul told us, on the authority of Ali bin Al-Aqmar, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas: that he recited this verse: Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects - you are not of them in anything, then he says: Your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is innocent of them. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father, Ibn Idris, Abu Usama, and Yahya Ibn Adam told us, on the authority of Malik Ibn Mughul, something similar. Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Hussein narrated to us, he said, Shuja Abu Badr narrated to us, on the authority of Amr bin Qais Al-Mala’i, he said, Umm Salamah said: Let a man fear that he will not be related to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in anything! Then she recited: Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects - you are not of them in anything. Amr bin Qais said: Al-Tayyib said it once, and he recited this verse. Abu Ja`far said: The correct statement in this regard is that his statement, You are not of them in anything, is an announcement from God to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he is innocent of the innovators of his nation who are heretics in his religion, and of the parties of the polytheists of his people, and of the Jews and Christians. And there is nothing in His announcement that would necessitate that he forbade him from fighting them, because it is not impossible to say in speech: You are not of the religion of the Jews and Christians in anything, so fight them, for their matter is up to God to bestow His favor upon whomever He wills among them and accept his repentance, and to destroy whomever He wills to destroy among them as a disbeliever, and to seize his soul, or to kill him with your hand in his disbelief, then to inform them of what they were doing when they came to Him. Since it was not impossible for the command to fight them to come together, and His saying: “You are not of them in anything. Their affair is with God,” and there was no clear evidence in the verse that it was abrogated, nor was there any report from the Messenger that it was abrogated, it was not permissible to rule that it was abrogated until a proof was established that would support the correctness of the statement, because we have explained that the abrogated is that which it is not permissible to come together with its abrogator in one situation, in our book: The Book of Al-Latif Min Al-Bayan ‘an Usul Al-Ahkam. As for His statement: Their affair is only with God, He is saying: I am the one to whom the affair of these polytheists who divided their religion and became sects, and the innovators from your nation who went astray from your path, is due, not to you and not to anyone else. Either by punishment if they persist in their misguidance and their religion divided them, so I will destroy them because of it, or by pardoning them through repentance and favor from Me to them. Then He will inform them of what they used to do, meaning: Then I will inform them in the Hereafter when they come to Me on the Day of Resurrection of what they used to do, so I will reward each of them for what they used to do in this world, the good among them for good, and the evildoer for evil. Then He, the Most High, informed of the extent of his reward for those who were rewarded with good or evil, saying: Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof, and whoever brings an evil deed will not be recompensed except the like thereof, and they will not be wronged.
6:160: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Whoever meets his Lord on the Day of Resurrection in the place of reckoning, from among those who left their religion and were sects, with repentance, faith, and abandoning what he was doing of his misguidance, and that is the good deed that God mentioned, saying: Whoever brings it will have ten times the like thereof. And what he means by his saying: He will have ten times the like thereof, he will have ten good deeds like the good deed he brought. And whoever brings evil, he says: And whoever of them meets on the Day of Resurrection having separated from those who are right and disbelieved in God, he will be recompensed only for what is bad for him as recompense, just as God recompensed him for his evil deeds. And they will not be wronged, he says: And God will not wrong the two groups, neither the group of good nor the group of evil, by rewarding the one who does good with evil and the one who does evil with good. Rather, He will reward each group with the recompense that is due to him, because He, may His praise be glorified, is wise and does not place anything except in the place in which it deserves to be placed, and He does not reward anyone except with the recompense he deserves. We have previously demonstrated that the meaning of injustice is to put something in the wrong place, with evidence that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. Abu Ja`far said: If someone were to say: If the matter is as you have mentioned, that the meaning of good in this context is belief in God, acknowledging His Oneness, and believing in His Messenger, and the meaning of bad in it is associating partners with Him and denying His Messenger, then does faith have examples for which the believer is rewarded? And if it has an example, then how is it rewarded, and faith, according to you, is only words and deeds, and the reward from God for His servants is honor for it in the Hereafter, and the favor upon him is what He has prepared for the people of His honor of bliss in the eternal home, and these are objects that are seen, witnessed, sensed and enjoyed, not words that are heard, nor the earnings of the limbs? It was said: The meaning of this is not what you have gone to. Rather, its meaning is: Whoever comes with a good deed and God fulfills it for him obediently, then he will have a reward equal to ten good deeds like it. If he said: I said: Is there any good deed like saying There is no god but God? It was said: It has something similar that is different from it, but it has something similar, which is the saying, There is no god but God, and that is what God, the Most High, promised whoever brings it to Him that He will reward him for it with a reward ten times that which its speaker deserves. And likewise it is for whoever brings the evil that is polytheism, except that He will not reward its doer for it except what he deserves for it without multiplying it for him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yaqub al-Qummi told us, on the authority of Ja`far ibn Abi al-Mughira, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, who said: When the verse, Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof, was revealed, a man from the people said: Is saying there is no god but God a good deed? He said: Yes, it is the best of good deeds. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hafs bin Ghayath told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash and Al-Hasan bin Ubaid God, on the authority of Jami’ bin Shaddad, on the authority of Al-Aswad bin Hilal, on the authority of Abdullah: Whoever brings a good deed, there is no god but God. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, Hafs told us, Al-A’mash and Al-Hasan bin Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Jami’ bin Shaddad, on the authority of Al-Aswad bin Hilal, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: Whoever brings a good deed, he said: Whoever brings There is no god but God. He said: And whoever brings an evil deed, he said: Polytheism. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Ubaid God, on the authority of Jami’ bin Shaddad, on the authority of Al-Aswad bin Hilal, on the authority of Abdullah: Whoever brings a good deed, he said: There is no god but God. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Amr Al-Ma’ni told us, on the authority of Zaidah, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Shaqiq: Whoever brings a good deed, he said: There is no god but God, the word of sincerity, and whoever brings an evil deed, he said: polytheism. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Saeed, and on the authority of Uthman ibn al-Aswad, on the authority of Mujahid and al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza: Whoever brings a good deed, they said: There is no god but God, the word of sincerity. And whoever brings an evil deed, they said: Polytheism and disbelief. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr and Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Abd al-Malik, on the authority of Ata’: Whoever brings a good deed, he said: There is no god but God, and whoever brings an evil deed, he said: Polytheism. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Jabir bin Nuh told us, he said, Musa bin Ubaidah told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b: Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof, he said: There is no god but God. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu al-Muhajjal, on the authority of Ibrahim: Whoever brings a good deed, he said: There is no god but God, and whoever brings an evil deed, he said: Polytheism. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Muhajjal, on the authority of Abu Ma’shar, on the authority of Ibrahim, the same. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Al-Muhajjal, on the authority of Ibrahim, the same. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Muhajjal, on the authority of Abu Ma’shar, he said: Ibrahim used to swear by God without concealing anything: Whoever brings a good deed, there is no god but God, and whoever brings an evil deed, whoever brings polytheism. Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Abdul Malik told us, on the authority of Ata’, regarding his statement: Whoever brings a good deed, he said: the word of sincerity, there is no god but God, and whoever brings an evil deed, he said: polytheism. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, and Al-Muthanna bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Abu Na’eem told us, all of them, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih: Whoever brings a good deed, he said: There is no god but God, and whoever brings an evil deed, he said: Polytheism. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Uthman ibn al-Aswad, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza: Whoever brings a good deed, he said: the word of sincerity, and whoever brings an evil deed, he said: disbelief. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Salamah, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: Whoever brings a good deed he said: There is no god but God. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of al-Hasan: Whoever brings a good deed, he said: There is no god but God. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed: Whoever brings a good deed, he said: There is no god but God. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Whoever brings a good deed, he said: whoever brings there is no god but God, and whoever brings an evil deed, he said: polytheism. Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid narrated, Saeed narrated, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof, and whoever brings an evil deed will not be recompensed except the like thereof, and they will not be wronged. He mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: “Actions are of six types: those that make things right and those that make things right, those that double and those that double, and like and like. As for the two that make things right: whoever meets God not associating anything with Him will enter Paradise, and whoever meets God associating anything with Him will enter Hell.” As for the two that make things right and like: the believer’s spending in the way of God is seven hundred times, and his spending on his family is ten times the like. As for like and like: if a servant intends to do a good deed but does not do it, a good deed is recorded for him, and if he intends to do a bad deed and then does it, a bad deed is recorded against him. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Shamr bin Atiyah, on the authority of a sheikh from the Taym, “On the authority of Abu Dharr, he said: I said: O Messenger of God, teach me an act that will bring me closer to Paradise and distance me from the Fire. He said: If you do a bad deed, then do a good deed, for it will be rewarded tenfold. I said: O Messenger of God, is ‘There is no god but God’ among the good deeds? He said: It is the best of good deeds.” Some people said: This verse refers to the Bedouins, but as for the immigrants, their good deeds are seven hundred times more. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Muadh bin Hisham told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu al-Siddiq al-Naji, on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, regarding his statement: Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof, he said: This is for the Bedouins, and for the emigrants it is seven hundred. Muhammad, Abu Nasheet bin Harun al-Harbi, said: Yahya bin Abi Bakr told us: Fadil bin Marzuq told us, on the authority of Atiyyah al-Awfi, on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar, who said: This verse was revealed about the Bedouins: Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof. A man said: What about the Muhajireen? He said: What is greater than that: “Indeed, God does not wrong by as much as an atom’s weight. And if there is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward.” When God says about something: Great, then it is great. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa`d told us, he said, Abu Ja`far told us, on the authority of al-Rabi`, he said: This verse was revealed: Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof, while they were fasting three days of the month and giving away one-tenth of their wealth. Then the obligatory duties were revealed after that: fasting Ramadan and zakat. If someone were to say: How was it said ten the like thereof, so that the ten was added to the likes, and they are the likes? And can a thing be added to itself? It was said: It was added to it because what was meant by it was: He has ten good deeds like it. So the examples took the place of the interpreter, and the ten was added to it, just as it is said: I have ten wives. So because the examples were intended to be their place, it was said: ten like it. So the ten was taken out, as the number of good deeds is taken out, and the example is masculine, not feminine. But when it was put in the place of good deeds, and the example is used for both masculine and feminine, so it was made a successor to it, what was mentioned was done to it. And whoever said: I have ten like it did not say: I have ten good deeds, because good deeds are an uncountable verb, but rather nouns are countable. And the example is a noun, and therefore the number is permissible with it. It was mentioned about Al-Hasan Al-Basri that he used to read this: He has ten with the tanween, and the like with the nominative. This is a correct reading in Arabic, but the reading in the countries is different from it, so we do not permit it to be different from what is agreed upon.
6:161: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these people who equate idols and statues with their Lord, Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, meaning: Say to them that my Lord has guided me to the straight path, which is the religion of God with which He sent me, and that is the Muslim Hanafi faith, so guide me to it, a straight religion, meaning: straight, the religion of Abraham, meaning: the religion of Abraham, Hanif, meaning: straight, and he was not of the polytheists, meaning: and he was not of the polytheists with God, meaning Abraham, may God bless him and grant him peace, because he was not of those who worshipped idols. The readings differed in the reading of His statement: a straight religion. The majority of the readers of Medina and some of the Basrans read it as a straight religion, with a fat-ha on the qaf and a shaddah on the ya’, linking it to the statement of God: That is the straight religion, and to His statement: That is the straight religion. The majority of the Kufian reciters read it as: Dīna Qayyimā with a kasra on the qaf, a fathah on the ya’ and a sukun on it. They said: Qayyim and Qayyim have the same meaning, and they are two languages that mean: the straight religion. Abu Jaafar said: The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings in the readings of the regions, and they agree in meaning. So whichever of them the reader reads, he is correct. However, opening the qaf and stressing the ya’ is more pleasing to me, because it is the more eloquent and well-known of the two languages. The accusative of his saying: in religion is based on the source of the meaning of his saying: Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, because the meaning is: My Lord has guided me to a sound religion, so I was guided to it a sound religion, so religion is accusative of the omitted word which is I was guided, which was replaced by his saying: Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path. Some of the people of Basra said: This is why he put it in the accusative case because when he said: My Lord has guided me to a straight path, he had informed us that he had known something, so he said: A straight religion, as if he had said: I have known a straight religion, the religion of Abraham. As for the meaning of al-Hanif, I have explained it in its place in Surat al-Baqarah with its evidence, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.
6:162: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to those who equate idols and statues with their Lord, who ask you to follow their desires in falsehood by worshipping gods and statues, Indeed, my prayer and my sacrifice, meaning: my sacrifice, and my life, meaning: my life, and my death, meaning: my death, are God, Lord of the worlds, meaning: that all of that is purely His, without what you, O polytheists, have associated with Him of idols, He has no partner in any of that of His creation, and none of them has a share in it, because it is not possible for that to be anything but purely His, and with this I have been commanded, meaning: with this my Lord has commanded me, and I am the first of the Muslims, meaning: and I am the first of this nation to acknowledge, submit, and submit to his Lord that it is thus. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. It was mentioned that the ritual, in this context, is slaughtering. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid: My prayer and my ritual, he said: The ritual is the sacrifices during Hajj and Umrah. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: And my sacrifice, my sacrifice in Hajj and Umrah. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And my sacrifice is my sacrifice in Hajj and Umrah. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ismail - not Ibn Abi Khalid - on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement: My prayer and my sacrifice, “My” means my sacrifice. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement: My prayer and my sacrifice, he said: My sacrifice. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr - Ibn Mahdi said: I do not know who this Ismail is! - My prayer and my sacrifice, he said: My prayer and my sacrifice. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement: My prayer and my sacrifice, he said: And my sacrifice. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, And my sacrifice, he said: my slaughter. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement: And my sacrifice, he said: My slaughter. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: My prayer and my ritual. He said: The prayer is the prayer, and the ritual is the slaughter.
6:163: As for his saying: And I am the first of the Muslims, then: Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And I am the first of the Muslims, he said: The first of the Muslims from this nation.
6:164: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to those who treat their idols as equals, who call you to worship idols and follow the footsteps of Satan, Shall I seek a lord other than God? He says: Should I seek a master other than God to rule over me? And He is the Lord of all things, He says: He is the Master of all things besides Him, its Manager and its Reformer. And no soul earns except against itself, He says: And no soul commits a sin except against itself, meaning: It is not held accountable for what it has done of disobedience to God Almighty, and what it has committed of sin, other than itself. Rather, every sinner is the one who is punished for his sin and taken for his guilt. And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another, He says: And no sinful soul shall bear the sin of another soul, but it shall bear the sin of its sin, and it shall be punished for it, not for the sin of another soul other than itself. What he means by that is the polytheists to whom God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say this. He says: Say to them: We are not held accountable for your sins, and you are responsible for your crimes, and we will have the reward for our deeds. This is like what God, may He be glorified, commanded him in another place to say to them: To you be your religion, and to me mine, and that is as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, he said: At that time, there was no way out for the scholars and worshippers except one of two choices, one of which was better than the other: either commanding and calling to the truth, or seclusion. Do not participate with the people of falsehood in their work, and perform the obligations between you and your Lord, and love for the sake of God and hate for the sake of God, and do not participate with anyone in sin. He said: A decisive verse was revealed concerning that: “Say: Shall I seek other than God as a Lord while He is the Lord of all things?” until His saying: In it you differ. And concerning that He said: And those who were given the Scripture did not become divided except after there came to them clear evidence. It is said of the burden: a burden that is burdened, a burden that is burdened, and a burden that is burdened, so he is burdened. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to these people who treat their Lord as equals, the idols: Every worker among us and among you will have the reward for his work, and upon him will be his burden, so do what you are doing. Then to your Lord, O people, is your return, meaning: then to Him is your destiny and your final destination. He will inform you of what you were in, in this world, differing in religions and sects, since some of you followed Judaism, some followed Christianity, some followed Zoroastrianism, and some worshipped idols and claimed partners with God and equals. Then He will reward all of you for what you did in this world, whether good or evil. Then you will learn who among us did good and who did evil.
6:165: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his nation: And God is He who made you, O people, successors on the earth, by destroying the generations and nations that came before you, and made you successors, and made you successors from among them on the earth, succeeding them in it and populating it after them. And successors is the plural of successor, just as wasathf is the plural of wasifa, and it is from the saying of the speaker: So-and-so succeeded so-and-so in his house, succeeding him as a successor, so he is a successor in it, as al-Shamakh said: Deaths befall them and I miss them, and I succeed in one region after another, and that is like: Al-Husayn told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And it is He who made you successors on the earth, he said: As for successors on the earth, He destroyed the generations and made us successors on it after them. As for his statement: And He raised some of you above others in degrees, he is saying: And He made your conditions different, so He made some of you above others, by raising this one over that one, by what He has spread for this one of provision, so He favored him with what He has given him of money and wealth, over this poor one in what He has given him of worldly causes, and this one over that one by what He has given him of strength and power over this weak, feeble, strong one. So He made them different, by raising one of the degrees above that of another, and lowering one of the degrees below that of this one, and that is like the one who: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: And He has raised some of you above others in degrees, meaning in provision. As for His statement, That He may test you in what He has given you, it means: To test you in what He has granted you of His bounty and bestowed upon you of His provision, so that He may know who among you is obedient to Him in what He has commanded him to do and what He has forbidden him to do, and who is disobedient? And who fulfills what He has given him of what He has commanded him to fulfill, and who is negligent in fulfilling it. Abu Ja`far said: God, the Most High, says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Indeed, your Lord, O Muhammad, is swift in punishing those who displease Him by committing sins and disobeying His commands and prohibitions, and those who test Him in what He has bestowed upon them of His grace and generosity, turning away from Him and turning away from Him, despite His favors upon them and His empowerment of them on earth, as He did with previous generations. And indeed, He is Forgiving, meaning: And He covers the sins of those who test Him by turning to Him in obedience when He tests them with His grace and tests them with His commands and prohibitions, so He covers them up and leaves their disgrace in the place of reckoning. Merciful by leaving His punishment for their previous sins that occurred between them and Him, when they repented and turned to Him before meeting Him and their final destination.
